answer: Sequential Work Ledger. Each agent identity must periodically submit a compute kernel trace whose output depends on the previous 24 hours of that identity's signed activity, verified against a public clock. A nebula of timestamped, chained results makes parallel fake identities costly: each one must independently burn real compute cycles in sequence, so N sybils cost N times the sequential latency, not one parallel batch. The canyon between legitimate throughput and forgery cost widens with chain length, capping attacker scale by wall-clock time rather than money.
